topicName: Variables, Scope, Precedence, and Fact Gathering
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: Variables, Scope, Precedence, and Fact Gathering in Ansible"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mastering how Ansible manages data is essential for writing scalable, maintainable, and predictable automation code. This tutorial covers variable definition, how scope affects visibility, how Ansible resolves conflicting values through precedence, and how fact gathering dynamically populates host data."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Variables and Scope"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Variables in Ansible allow you to manage differences between your managed nodes. Variables can be defined at various scopes: global (configured in ansible.cfg or command line), play (defined within a play), and host (defined in inventory or host_vars)."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"--- 
- name: Example Playbook
  hosts: webservers
  vars:
    http_port: 80
  tasks:
    - name: Ensure apache is running
      ansible.builtin.service:
        name: apache2
        state: started"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Ansible Variable Precedence"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"When the same variable is defined in multiple places, Ansible uses a strict order of precedence to determine which value to use. A later item in the precedence list overrides earlier items. For example, extra vars (-e) always override all other definitions."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"1. command line extra vars (-e) [highest precedence]"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"2. task vars (only for the task)"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"3. block vars (only for tasks in block)"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"4. play vars and role vars"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"5. inventory variables and host_vars/group_vars [lowest precedence]"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Fact Gathering"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Fact gathering is the process where Ansible automatically queries managed nodes for system properties (such as IP addresses, operating systems, and available memory) before executing tasks. These facts are stored in variables prefixed with ansible_."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"--- 
- name: Display gathered facts
  hosts: all
  gather_facts: true
  tasks:
    - name: Print the IP address
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "The IP address is {{ ansible_default_ipv4.address }}""},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Optimizing Fact Gathering"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Gathering facts for every host can slow down large deployments. You can disable fact gathering by setting gather_facts: false, or you can cache facts to improve playbook execution speed across runs."}]
